cards.name: Kevin Lyons
cards.job_title: Professor of Professional Practice, Department of Supply Chain Management
cards.organization: Rutgers Business School–Newark and New Brunswick
cards.could_speak_on: How local and regenerative sourcing can be built into procurement systems and assessed for environmental, economic, and community impacts.
talk_ideas: Embedding environmental and social criteria in procurement
Local sourcing networks and supply-chain resilience
Supply-chain archaeology and product end-of-life research
cards.bio: Kevin Lyons is a Professor of Professional Practice in Rutgers Business School’s Department of Supply Chain Management and directs its Public Private Community Partnership Program. His research includes integrating environmental, social, health, and economic criteria into supply chains, procurement, and contracting, as well as developing local sourcing networks.
credentials: Developed the Supply Chain Archaeology research discipline
Recipient of the Sierra Club Annual Professional of the Year Award and the New Jersey Governor’s Award for Environmental Leadership and Excellence
cards.why_fit: His academic research and applied work connect procurement, local sourcing, environmental criteria, and community economic development—directly relevant to scaling regenerative sourcing.

past_speaking.event: ARIS Summit 2026 keynote: “Supply Chains for Society: Quantifying Impact by Design”

notable_work: Books: Buying for the Future; Contract Management and the Environmental Challenge (2000)
A Roadmap to Green Supply Chains: Using Supply Chain Archaeology and Big Data Analytics (2015)
cards.fit_reason: Strong academic and practical match for regenerative sourcing at scale, with a confirmed research and procurement focus and a documented keynote appearance.
